description: Stages a post of one of this account's finished videos to one of its connected TikTok, YouTube or Instagram accounts and returns the post id `publish_post` takes. NOTHING IS PUBLISHED BY THIS CALL. WHEN: after `list_social_accounts` gave you an account id and you have a finished video's id (`list_videos` / `get_video`, `status` `succeeded`). AN AI VIDEO STORY EPISODE MUST BE RENDERED FIRST: it reports `succeeded` at `story.stage: "ready_to_render"`, where its only file is the raw stitched preview, and an unrendered episode is REFUSED (409 `episode_not_rendered`): call `render_story_video`, wait for `story.stage: "rendered"`, then prepare. IF THE USER IS LOOKING AT A RENDERED CARD, DO NOT ASK THEM TO CONFIRM IN CHAT: call `review_post` with the id this returns and STOP. The card shows the actual video, the destination account and the caption, visibility and disclosure controls, and the person confirms there; reciting `account_limits` and asking 'public or friends-only?' is what it replaces. WHY TWO STEPS: on TikTok this call asks the platform what the user's own account allows and returns it as `account_limits` (the privacy levels it may use; whether comments, duet or stitch are off): show the user those options, get their choice, and only then call `publish_post`. A prepared post expires after 30 minutes because those limits can change. On YouTube and Instagram nothing is asked of the platform (`account_limits` says `source: aicut_api_limits`): do not present it as what the channel allows. FIELDS ARE PER PLATFORM (each field says which; another platform's is refused). Instagram: `trial_graduation_strategy` makes a trial reel. The caption is sent exactly as given (refused, never trimmed). `is_your_brand` and `is_branded_content` are TikTok's commercial-disclosure declarations (the user's own business; a paid partnership). Both default to false: set one only if the USER told you to, because a disclosure they did not make must not be sent for them. `schedule_at` stages a post for later (ISO-8601, 10 minutes to a year ahead); `publish_post` commits it. ASK THE USER FOR A TIME rather than inventing one, and say what scheduling means on their platform (the account's `schedule_custody`). You can only post a video on this aicut account (by id, never a url: `import_video` brings an outside clip in), to a social account this same user connected. REFUSALS you act on: 403 `insufficient_scope` = THE USER'S CONNECTION CANNOT POST (it was approved before aicut added the `social:publish` permission), so a connection that generates videos fine can still be refused here. It is not an outage and not a bad `video_id` or `account_id`; a retry, another account or another video cannot fix it. Tell the user to disconnect aicut at https://www.aicut.pro/account/settings#connections, connect it again and approve "Post your videos to your connected social accounts" (generating stops working until they have reconnected), then STOP.

caption.description: The post text exactly as given: up to 2200 characters; on YouTube the DESCRIPTION, up to 5000.

category_id.description: YouTube only: the category id. Default 24 (Entertainment).

is_branded_content.description: TikTok disclosure: a paid partnership. Default false; set only if the user said so.

is_your_brand.description: TikTok disclosure: the user's own business. Default false; set only if the user said so.

platform.description: The platform to post to; it must match the `platform` of the account id (the platforms number accounts independently).

privacy_level.description: TikTok: one of `account_limits.privacy_level_options` (PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE, MUTUAL_FOLLOW_FRIENDS, FOLLOWER_OF_CREATOR, SELF_ONLY): ask the user. YouTube: public, unlisted or private. Required on both.

schedule_at.description: ISO-8601. Omit to publish when `publish_post` is called.

tags.description: YouTube only: up to 30 tags, 500 characters in total.

title.description: YouTube only, required: the title, up to 100 characters.

trial_graduation_strategy.description: Instagram only: post a trial reel, shown to non-followers first. SS_PERFORMANCE: shared to followers if it performs well; MANUAL: a trial until shared in the Instagram app. Set only if the user asked for a trial or test reel.

video_id.description: The id of a FINISHED (episode: RENDERED) video on this account, or an `import_video` id.

name: prepare_post
title: Prepare a social post
